pr_title: fix(ngcc): switch ngcc over to use the `TraitCompiler`
pr_body:
fix(ngcc): do not attempt compilation when analysis fails

In #34288, ngtsc was refactored to separate the result of the analysis
and resolve phase for more granular incremental rebuilds. In this model,
any errors in one phase transition the trait into an error state, which
prevents it from being ran through subsequent phases. The ngcc compiler
on the other hand did not adopt this strict error model, which would
cause incomplete metadata—due to errors in earlier phases—to be offered
for compilation that could result in a hard crash.

This commit updates ngcc to take advantage of ngtsc's `TraitCompiler`,
that internally manages all Ivy classes that are part of the
compilation. This effectively replaces ngcc's own `AnalyzedFile` and
`AnalyzedClass` types, together with all of the logic to drive the
`DecoratorHandler`s. All of this is now handled in the `TraitCompiler`,
benefiting from its explicit state transitions of `Trait`s so that the
ngcc crash is a thing of the past.

Fixes #34500
Resolves FW-1788
pr_comments: This PR is a replacement for #34652, with a different approach. Instead of making use of the `Trait`  types from within ngcc, this change goes one step further to drive the compilation using the `TraitCompiler`. The benefit of this is that the protocol around the calling of `DecoratorHandlers` isn't duplicated between ngtsc and ngcc, with the drawback of introducing a larger diff with more risk involved.

This is green on CI: angular/ngcc-validation#792

@petebacondarwin PTAL

review_comments:
That is indeed much nicer but when I applied this change I noticed that `renderInfo` is only available in the loop. I tried to introduce

```ts
      let dtsRenderInfo: DtsRenderInfo|null = null;
```

instead of `addReexports` to capture the render info, but then you'd need to workaround a TS limitation where it doesn't recognize that `dtsRenderInfo` could have been reassigned within the closure, so it would narrow `dtsRenderInfo` to `never` after a `dtsRenderInfo !== null`. At that point I don't think the readability is better than what it currently is, so I kept it unchanged.

I know that splice is probably more efficient but since this is just a test, perhaps 

```ts
analyzer.handlers = [...analyzer.handlers, testHandler];
```

is a bit more reasonable?

OOC Can you explain why we cannot just wipe out the standard handlers for this test?

Oooh, so this is actually trickier than it looks (and perhaps even trickier than it should be, honestly). The `analyze.handlers` is passed into the `NgccTraitCompiler` and is shared through the array reference. Replacing the array would therefore not make the new handlers available to the trait compiler.

If I just append/prepend the handler some tests start to fail, hence the `slice`.

Oh! I forgot that the second parameter is the `delete`, which means that my suggestion is incorrect.
Perhaps a comment in the code to stop people like me from worrying about it?

Can you add a jsdoc description of this method since, unlike the `DefaultMigrationHost` it cannot fallback on the decription in the base `MigrationHost` interface. Copying the one from that interface would be fine by me (although that is also missing explanation of the `flags` param!):

```
  /**
   * Associate a new synthesized decorator, which did not appear in the original source, with a
   * given class.
   * @param clazz the class to receive the new decorator.
   * @param decorator the decorator to inject.
   */
   ```
Here I do actually prefer the early `continue`, as I usually deal with "edge-cases" with an early control flow statement to keep the main body of work at the top.

It seems to me that most of this spec file is actually testing the `NgccTraitCompiler`. The `DefaultMigrationHost` mostly just delegates to that.

How about simplifying this spec just to check that the delegation occurs as expected, and then create a spec for `NgccTraitCompiler` that exercises the tests here?

I'm really not fond of testing just delegation behaviour, as doing so starts to be testing an implementation rather than some desired behaviour. I do see however where you're coming from here, and have moved most of the `injectSyntheticDecorator` and `getAllDecorators` tests to an `NgccTraitCompiler` spec file, while retaining some in the `DefaultMigrationHost` specs to test the logic in the context of the migration host.
I know this had none before, but some jsdoc descriptions of this interface and its fields would be great!
